The '''Kaup–Kupershmidt equation''' (named after David J. Kaup and Boris Abram Kupershmidt) is the [[nonlinear partial differential equation|nonlinear]] fifth-order [[partial differential equation]]

:<math>u_t = u_{xxxxx}+10u_{xxx}u+25u_{xx}u_x+20u^2u_x = \frac16 (6u_{xxxx}+60uu_{xx}+45u_x^2+40u^3)_x. </math>

It is the first equation in a hierarchy of [[integrable system|integrable equations]] with the [[Lax pair|Lax operator]]

:<math> \partial_x^3 + 2u\partial_x + u_x, </math> .

It has properties similar (but not identical) to those of the better-known [[Korteweg–de Vries equation|KdV hierarchy]] in which the Lax operator has order 2.
